extracted.intended_audience: general public, stakeholders, and participants in U.S. federal rulemaking (citizens, practitioners, students)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the U.S. federal rulemaking process (particularly informal notice-and-comment rulemaking), the public participation framework, procedural steps from proposed rule to codification, and what public comments accomplish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The public receives advance notice of proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice gives stakeholders opportunity to learn about proposals before finalization; notice is typically published in the Federal Register as part of the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for written public comment and data submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens can submit written comments and provide data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments allow citizens to contribute information, data, and perspectives to the rulemaking record that agencies may lack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of the rulemaking record
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking record becomes publicly accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transparent, public record lets stakeholders review the materials that informed the agency's decision and enables later public or judicial scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency obligation to analyze and respond to public input
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must analyze and respond to public input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are required to consider comments and incorporate analysis of them into the administrative record; this obligation supports accountability and enables judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent documentation trail
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent documentation trail is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking maintains a documented history of proposals, comments, analyses, and decisions so the process and agency reasoning are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected parties can seek review in courts to challenge agency rules or the adequacy of the agency's consideration of comments and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of proposed rule with justification and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule in Federal Register with justification and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed rule must be published with the agency's justification and supporting analysis so the public can evaluate and comment on the substance and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period (duration varies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Comment Period (30-180 days depending on complexity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment periods commonly range from about 30 to 180 days depending on complexity; length affects stakeholders' ability to prepare substantive input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response requirement (must address issues raised)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Response — must address every issue raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing the final rule, agencies must respond to significant comments and explain how the input affected their decisions; failure to address issues can be grounds for challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rule publication with comment responses and updated analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Rule — published with comment responses, updated analysis, final language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule should incorporate or respond to relevant comments, update analyses as needed, and present the definitive regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication, final rules are codified in the Code of Federal Regulations for long-term regulatory effect and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments supply factual data agencies may lack
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments provide the agency with data it may lack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-supported comments can fill informational gaps in the agency record, supplying empirical evidence, technical data, or practical experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments identify gaps in agency analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters can point out analytical omissions, methodological weaknesses, or neglected considerations the agency should address before finalizing a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments create an official record the agency must address
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments create an official record the agency must address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By entering information into the administrative record, comments obligate agencies to consider and respond to those points in their decision-making and written responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal rulemaking (notice-and-comment) as the standard process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most federal rulemaking follows the informal notice-and-comment model, which emphasizes publication of a proposal, public comment, and reasoned agency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid rulemaking (formal hearings when authorized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid rulemaking — formal hearing procedures with cross-examination, only when Congress specifically authorizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid or formal procedures (e.g., on-the-record hearings with cross-examination) are not standard and occur only where statute requires or permits them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of roles between Congress and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress establishes broad policy mandates; agencies develop detailed rules with scientific and technical expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative bodies set the broad policy framework while agencies, with technical expertise, fill in detailed regulatory requirements through rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing expert agency decision-making with democratic accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism balances expert agency decision-making with democratic accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice-and-comment rulemaking is designed to harness agency expertise while providing public participation to ensure democratic legitimacy and oversight.
